name: HI-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
model.rationale: The district's D+12 lean, incumbent Tokuda's dominant fundraising edge, and markets pricing her win at roughly 95% all point to a comfortable Democratic hold. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays near the baseline.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Republican Brenton Awa closing within single digits, or unexpected outside spending, would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Hawaii's second district is a solidly Democratic seat, with a partisan lean of about twelve points toward Democrats. Incumbent Jill Tokuda is running for reelection after clearing her primary, and she holds a large financial advantage, having raised over $820,000 with more than $570,000 on hand. Republican Brenton Awa has raised only about $123,000 and has minimal cash remaining, with no reported outside spending on either side.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets give Tokuda roughly a 95% chance of winning. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and the money gap points to a comfortable Democratic victory, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
